metadata.description: Standards bypass configuration for prax branch

bypass.reason: This IS the display handler layer. unified_stream.py is the designated terminal output formatter for the monitoring system. console.print() is its core responsibility, not a violation.
Prax import chain — transitively imported by logger.py. Cannot import from aipass.prax.apps.modules.logger (circular dependency).

The fleet json service (DPLAN-0325) is stdlib-only by contract: it must import without pulling the prax logger graph (30 modules, watchdog, the aipass.trigger edge), which is the entire point of the lazy package init. A test pins the cold import footprint at 6 aipass modules and zero third-party.
Prax import chain — directly imported by logger.py. Cannot import from aipass.prax.apps.modules.logger (circular dependency).
Prax import chain — imported via logging/lifecycle.py. Cannot import from aipass.prax.apps.modules.logger (circular dependency).
Prax import chain — directly imported by logger.py. Cannot import from aipass.prax.apps.modules.logger (circular dependency).
Prax import chain — imported via discovery/watcher.py. Cannot import from aipass.prax.apps.modules.logger (circular dependency).

Prax import chain — imported by config/load.py, which logger.py calls while CONSTRUCTING the system logger. Cannot import from aipass.prax.apps.modules.logger (circular dependency), and a diagnostic that needs the logger it is being emitted from is a second crash wearing a diagnostic's clothes (@memory, 2026-08-31). A test pins that this module imports nothing from aipass at all.
Architectural — imports config.load (shared infrastructure) and trigger.modules.core (optional cross-branch integration with graceful fallback).
Architectural — imports config.load (shared infrastructure), trigger (optional integration), and uses module_name parameter for explicit caller attribution in monitoring context.

Architectural — imports config.load (shared infrastructure) and uses module_name parameter for explicit direct-logging binding. Auto-detection is the default (get_direct_logger()), but the internal class accepts explicit names for infrastructure callers.
Architectural — imports discovery/scanner for module discovery during logging lifecycle management. Uses module_name parameter for explicit lifecycle control of named modules.

Architectural — logging infrastructure imports config.load for path configuration. Uses module_name parameter for explicit logger setup per-module. Auto-detection is not appropriate for a setup function that configures loggers for specified modules.
Architectural — imports PRAX_JSON_DIR from config.load (shared infrastructure). Uses module_name parameter for explicit filter context from callers.

Monitor is a 3-thread architecture (display, file watcher, log watcher) that is tightly coupled by design. The threads share state (queues, positions dict, stop events) making splitting impractical without introducing complex inter-module synchronization. Direct JSON read of registry at line 344 is a one-time startup operation for branch discovery — routing through json_handler would add unnecessary dependency for a simple registry read.
False positive — stdlib imports (lines 49-55) are correctly before aipass imports (lines 58+). Checker misidentifies docstring content as import lines.
False positive — placeholder class methods inside except block detected as missing docstrings.
Redundant prefix in filename — monitoring_filters.py in monitoring/ dir. Renaming to filters.py would break existing imports across multiple files. Deferred to avoid churn.

False positive — logger_key, target, sys_limits, backupCount, encoding, local_limits, key are local variables inside functions, not module-level constants. backupCount follows logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler parameter naming.

Architectural — _original_getLogger and _original_basicConfig store references to stdlib functions (camelCase follows stdlib naming). enhanced_getLogger wraps logging.getLogger (matching stdlib convention).
False positive — _terminal_output_enabled and _terminal_module_available are mutable flags set conditionally, not constants.
on_created() is a watchdog.FileSystemEventHandler callback — called by watchdog.Observer at runtime, not by name in branch code.
on_created(), on_modified(), on_deleted(), on_moved() are watchdog.FileSystemEventHandler callbacks — called by watchdog.Observer at runtime via method dispatch.
on_modified() is a watchdog.FileSystemEventHandler callback — called by watchdog.Observer at runtime when log files change.
on_created(), on_modified(), on_deleted(), on_moved() are watchdog.FileSystemEventHandler callbacks — called by watchdog.Observer at runtime via method dispatch.
run_monitoring_loop() is the handler entry point for continuous monitoring — designed to be called by the logger module or daemon processes as a long-running loop.

initialize_logging_system() and shutdown_logging_system() are public API lifecycle functions exported in __all__ — designed to be called by other branches and entry points to start/stop the logging system.

Intentional — status is a leaf command where bare invocation shows system status (the primary user intent), not module introspection. Introspection is available via print_introspection() and __main__.

Template files managed by spawn — prax cannot add/remove them. Template structure is defined in spawn/templates/builder/ and applied at branch creation. Measured 2026-08-13: suppresses exactly one finding, the missing artifacts/birth_certificate.json. Narrowed from file='apps/', which the substring matcher spread over all 74 apps/ files.

Deliberate 4th layer, not a layering breach. apps/plugins/devpulse_dashboard/ holds per-branch dashboard sections (git, session, dispatch) loaded by devpulse, documented in README. The 3-layer check reads them as misplaced. Measured 2026-08-13: 3 files (dispatch_section, git_section, refresh). Split out of the old file='apps/' rule, whose stated reason was about spawn templates and never described these.

queue.Empty is expected control flow from PriorityQueue.get(timeout=N), not an error. Logging it produces 144,000 noise entries per 4hrs of monitoring (10 polls/sec). The empty state IS the normal idle state.

This IS the display handler for the commons live feed (DPLAN-0257). commons_feed.py is a self-contained view — polling, formatting, and terminal rendering together, same shape as unified_stream.py. console.print() is its designated purpose, not a violation.

Pure argument-inspection predicate — no I/O, no state, no branch imports by design. Runs on every command invocation, so log_operation() here would write a line per CLI call and drown the operation log prax itself is meant to keep readable. Same rule and same measured reason adopted by @memory, @trigger, @drone and @ai_mail for their help_flags handlers (convention settled 2026-08-13, DPLAN-0291 rule E).

The path is pinned by the DPLAN-0325 spec (section 1) and hashed by seedgo's acceptance: 'src/aipass/prax/apps/handlers/json/json_service.py'. Renaming it to service.py forks the one contract file the whole fleet reads. The prefix is not redundant either — json_service.py and json_handler.py (the shim) sit in the same directory and 'service.py' would not say which service.

Reached by string, not by an import statement: aipass/prax/__init__.py resolves it with importlib.import_module inside its PEP 562 __getattr__, which is what keeps the module out of every consumer's import graph until it is asked for. A scan keyed on import statements cannot see that edge. The entry point 'from aipass.prax import json_handler' is the fleet's only sanctioned import.

Shim pattern — module-level names are BOUND METHODS of the fleet json service's JsonHandle, not constants. Lowercase is correct for callable bindings, and the file is byte-identical in all 18 branches by the owner's ruling (2026-09-03), hashed by seedgo. Matches the identical bypass in spawn/, canary/ and memory/.

prax, leg 7: a two-line package init (`from . import handlers`), not an entry point; it parses no argv. The entry point is apps/prax.py, which takes --version/-V (argparse, and TOP_LEVEL_OPTIONS). The check names no line, so the rule is file-wide on this file alone.

prax, leg 7: True is the handler contract's 'this module owned the command', not an answer. The failure reaches the caller through error() on the line above, which is what marks the run failed for the exit seam in prax.py main(). The checker's error() exemption reads a success-path return, not the handler's own.

prax, leg 7: same contract as status.py:132. The router's True means a module owned the command, as its docstring says, and the failure is reported through error() on the line above, which sets the exit code.

prax, leg 7: True is the command's 'handled'. The failure was already shown to the operator through error() two lines above (then the relay is stopped), the same as the db-missing guard's return True; error() is what marks the run failed.

prax, leg 7: 'unknown' means one thing on both paths, as the docstring says: there is no module behind frame 2. sys._getframe raises ValueError exactly when the stack is too shallow to have that frame; it is the same answer, not a failure dressed as one.

prax, leg 7: the docstring names None as the answer 'the caller cannot be located — an answer, not a failure'. A path that will not resolve is a caller that cannot be located; branch detection is a routing hint and must never raise into the caller's import.

prax, leg 7: these are display labels and detector hints, and the value means the same on both paths. None at 392/423 is 'this detector has no answer, try the next' (an unreadable passport falls back to path matching, a file outside ~/Projects is not an external project); 'UNKNOWN' at 604/662/701 is the label for 'branch not determined', which is true when detection failed. The event is still displayed either way; no caller acts on the difference.

prax, leg 7: None means 'this session file names no working directory', which is what an unreadable session file tells the caller as well; the caller then labels the event by the next means. The read is a display hint and the failure is logged at the line above.

prax, leg 10 (file-wide: this checker passes no line). The sleeps at 433-475 belong to the two TestDispatcherSurvivesHandlerFailure tests, whose subject is a real watchdog dispatcher thread surviving a file that vanishes before its stat and then still draining its queue. The race lives in the observer's own thread over real time; there is no event to wait on that the product exposes, and a wait seam in the watcher would be a door for this test alone.

prax, leg 10 (file-wide: this checker passes no line; the one patch is at 741). The subject is how many times the handler stats one file per event. Path.stat is wrapped, not replaced: the wrapper counts calls on that one path and returns the real answer for every path, for the test's span only (monkeypatch). A stat seam in the handler would be a door for this test alone.

prax, leg 14. These calls were always here; the _load helper hid them from the checker until this leg bound the modules by import. The file's subject is four copies of one quick_status calculator, and the defect it pins is the drift between them, so each copy is called by name in the parametrize table; a public door mixes in the merge and the other writers and could not tell which copy drifted. The other private calls the helper hid (the pusher's structural step, the differ's per-branch diff) now go through push_dashboard_template and diff_dashboard_template on a tmp world.

prax, leg 14. 320: the walk on the OTHER platform's dialect (a drive-qualified Windows path, from a Linux run). source_root makes a host Path of its start, so only the pure walk can take that dialect; the host's own dialect goes through source_root in the three tests above it. 842: load's lane of the repo root; its one public reader, get_system_logs_dir outside a pytest session, ends in a mkdir of the live system_logs, so the lane is asked by name (prax, leg 5, HELD; re-read this leg, unchanged).

prax, leg 10. 109: the autouse fixture resets the relay's backoff to its starting value, which the module keeps only in _BACKOFF_INITIAL; copying the number would let the reset drift from the product. 425: _render_event is the one point where an event fans out to the relay and the console; the only public route to it is 'monitor run', a live loop on real watchers and the real relay, so the test calls the fan-out with both sinks doubled. Mutants: order swapped and relay argument changed both die at the assert.

prax, leg 10 (file-wide: this checker passes no line). Three families, each a with-block undone at its end. Path.home: _get_watch_directories reads ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions, and without the patch the test would walk the operator's live session trees; it answers tmp_path. time.sleep: the monitor loops pace themselves with time.sleep(0.1/0.5); the doubles end the loop (KeyboardInterrupt) or count turns, and a clock seam would be a door for the tests alone. sys.stdin.isatty and builtins.input: the interactive prompt reads the terminal; the tests choose the TTY branch and feed lines or EOF, where a reader seam would be a door for the tests alone.

prax, leg 11, under devpulse's console ruling (b): the colour is the claim (error level red, SEEDGO green, an unknown branch white), and it exists nowhere but inside print_event's console call (a dict lookup into the markup string). capsys strips it. A real Console on a buffer with colour forced, set by monkeypatch for the three colour tests alone; every other test in the file reads the real console with capsys.

prax, leg 11 (file-wide: this checker passes no line; the patches are at 89, 104, 127). The subject is the growth rate between two scans, which scan_rates measures with time.time(). The tests move the clock 10 s forward for the second scan, in a with-block undone at its end; waiting 10 real seconds is the only alternative, and a clock seam in rate_tracker would be a door for the tests alone.

prax, leg 11 (file-wide: this checker passes no line; the one patch is at 588). The subject is that a path that will not resolve (resolve raising OSError, as a deleted cwd does) answers None and never takes down the caller's import. No platform makes Path.resolve raise on demand under tmp_path; monkeypatch undoes it at the test's end.

prax, leg 11 (file-wide: this checker passes no line; the one patch is at 928). The subject is initialize_positions surviving a .log file whose stat fails. The wrapper raises only for .log paths and returns the real stat for every other path, in a with-block; no platform makes stat fail on demand on a file that exists.

prax, leg 11 (file-wide: this checker passes no line; the patches are at 358, 375, 393). The subject is the atomic write's retry on a Windows sharing violation: os.replace raising PermissionError while another process holds the target. Linux never raises it, so the double raises it a set number of times and then does the real replace; monkeypatch undoes it at the test's end.

prax, leg 11 (file-wide: this checker passes no line; the patches are at 118-119 and 777-778 since prax, leg 13). The subject is the handler surviving a rollover that fails on a full or locked disk; doRollover is made to raise the test's own OSError, in a with-block. No platform fails a rollover on demand under tmp_path. The sys.stderr patch at 862 was cured to capsys this leg.

prax, leg 10 (file-wide: this checker passes no line; the patches are at 62-107 and 171). The subject is try_acquire's liveness verdict, which branches on sys.platform and asks os.kill(pid, 0) on POSIX. The patches pin each branch on every CI platform and assert the pid passed; a real os.kill would signal a real process, and a platform or kill seam in the lock would be a door for the tests alone. Line 171 makes the /proc boot-id read fail the way a platform without /proc does. Each patch is a with-block, undone at its end.

prax, leg 10 (file-wide: this checker passes no line; the patches are at 64-65 and 115-116). The subject is the POSIX /proc liveness branch, chosen by sys.platform at call time. The tests pin that branch on every CI platform; Path.exists is wrapped to answer for the one /proc pid and fall through to the real call otherwise. A platform seam in pid_cache would be a door for the tests alone. Each patch is a with-block, undone at its end.

notes.usage: Add entries to 'bypass' list to exclude specific violations

fields.standard: Standard name: cli, error_handling, log_visibility, handlers, etc. (required)
fields.lines: Optional - specific line numbers to bypass

architectural_notes.prax_import_chain: logger.py imports from: logging/setup.py, logging/introspection.py, logging/override.py, logging/direct.py, discovery/watcher.py, registry/load.py, config/load.py, json/json_handler.py. These files (and their transitive imports) cannot import from aipass.prax.apps.modules.logger without circular dependency.
architectural_notes.config_as_shared_infra: config/load.py provides shared constants (ECOSYSTEM_ROOT, PRAX_ROOT, path helpers) used by nearly all prax handlers. It is intentionally shared infrastructure, not an encapsulation boundary.
architectural_notes.trigger_integration: Several handlers optionally import trigger.modules.core for event firing. All have graceful ImportError fallbacks. This is cross-branch integration, not an architectural violation.
